submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires where a sentence stops merely mentioning something and starts characterising it: the slot just before a predicate nominal after a copula or copula-like verb ('the film was a disaster', 'the memo was a clear example', 'This paper offers an analysis', 'counted as a clear sign'), after an as/like construal ('widely seen as a turning point', 'read him like an open scroll', 'more than just a marker'), or after a minimiser that reduces a subject to a bare category ('merely', 'just', 'only', 'simply', 'nothing but', 'no more than'). It does not care which noun fills the slot (swapping 'example' for 'photo', 'table', 'disaster' or 'evidence' leaves the peak unchanged) and the same noun phrase in subject or object position is nearly silent, so the mechanism is retrospective: it reads the ascriptive frame already built by the preceding words, while its Jacobian lens and ablation read out the abstract characterisation nouns that typically fill such a slot (evidence, example, indication, acknowledgment, manifestation, testimony) rather than one specific upcoming token.

rival_explanations: A broad prenominal-slot neuron: the real trigger is the function word that opens a noun phrase anywhere in the clause (a, an, some, their, his, mere, usual, vivid), and the ascriptive examples only dominate the scan because expository text has many predicate nominals - it predicts the same firing when that noun phrase is a subject or an object.

A minimiser/exclusive detector: the pole tracks the lexical class {mere, merely, just, only, simply, but, some, no more than} rather than any predication, so it should fire just as hard when such a word modifies a verb or an adjective ('he merely glanced', 'merely tired') and stay quiet on 'was a disaster' or 'seen as a turning point' where no minimiser occurs.

A lookahead neuron preparing the evidence/testimony noun family, since the Jacobian lens and the pole's ablation both push exactly those nouns and the peak sits one or two tokens before the noun would land - it predicts that swapping the head noun after the slot changes the activation, which is the discriminator this hypothesis denies.

top_examples.text:
While Face ID, Apple’s native facial recognition technology, is one of the key compelling features of the iPhone X, it seems to have some loopholes. Some security researchers have already claimed to have fooled Face ID with 3D-printed masks. And now, a mother and her 10-year-old son show how Face ID can be fooled, failing to secure the experience between family members.
This is what a new video shows that features Sana Sherwani and her kid Ammar Malik. The 41-second-long video shows that the kid was easily able to unlock the iPhone X of Sherwani – there is some visible family resemblance, but some rather distinct facial features as well.
Attaullah Malik, the husband of Sherwani, pointed out some flaws in a LinkedIn post that led his son to unlock the iPhone X of his wife. “Apparently, TrueDepth camera’s depth map of my wife’s face, which was created by projecting and analysing over 30,000 dots, wasn’t accurate enough as it worked with my 10-year-old son. He doesn’t fall under the ‘twins’ exception and has a big age difference compared to my wife. His face is smaller than my wife’s face, and the geometry of their faces don’t match, at least to human eyes,” writes Malik, who works as a director of technology operations at Taskstream.
If in case Face ID doesn’t recognise a face, it presents a passcode input to users. If the failed scan passed a certain threshold of resemblance, and the passcode is inputted correctly thereafter, Face ID takes another scan to correct its model in the attempt to be more accurate in the future. Apple in its security white paper says this “augmentation process” for its Face ID model is to “keep up with dramatic changes in your facial hair or makeup use, while minimising false acceptance. However, Malik claims this wasn’t the case with his wife and son, and no-one entered the passcode after Face ID rejected a scan, Wired reports.
Although family members can be an exception in case of protecting the iPhone X using Face ID, a group of Vietnamese researchers recently claimed that they had fooled the same authentication system using a composite 3D-printed mask. Apple assured users at the iPhone X launch that Face ID can differentiate masks and real human faces. But the researchers’ team at security firm Bkav allegedly proved that assurance wrong through a mask that cost $150 (approximately Rs. 9,800) to make.

You're Mine (Eternal)

"You're Mine (Eternal)" is a song by American singer and songwriter Mariah Carey included on her fourteenth studio album, Me. I Am Mariah... The Elusive Chanteuse (2014). It premiered on February 12, 2014, as the third single from the album. It was written and produced by Carey with Rodney Jerkins. An R & B song, the lyrics revolve around the singer reminiscing about a past lover. Critical response to the song was positive: Carey's breathy vocal style and use of the whistle register at the climax earned praise from critics. It also garnered several comparisons to one of Carey's previous singles, "We Belong Together" (2005).

In the United States, "You're Mine (Eternal)" reached number 88 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, but it experienced greater success on the Dance Club Songs chart, becoming her seventeenth number-one song. Elsewhere, it reached the top 20 in Hungary and on the UK R & B Chart and the top 30 in Spain. Carey co-directed the music video with photographer Indrani, which depicted the singer as a mermaid swimming around the lakes at the El Yunque National Forest in Puerto Rico. Recording artist Trey Songz appears as a love interest in the video. He also features on the urban remix of the song, performing his verses in the remix video. Carey has performed the song at the BET Honors and during a performance at the Empire State Building.

Background and release

On December 31, 2013, Carey appeared on NBC's New Year's Eve with Carson Daly show to perform some songs. Before giving the audience some advice on love for 2014 and prior to singing "The Art of Letting Go" from Me. I Am Mariah... The Elusive Chanteuse, the singer announced that she would be releasing a new single on February 14, 2014, to coincide with Valentine's Day. On February 12, Carey released "You're Mine (Eternal)" as the album's third single. The single's artwork consists of Sweethearts, a brand of sugar candies.

In the United States, the song was released to contemporary, rhythmic, and urban adult contemporary radio stations around the country on February 18. An urban remix featuring vocals by American recording artist Trey Songz was also made available to download digitally on February 13. In an interview with MTV News, Carey praised Songz vocal ability, saying that most artists are not able to sing and rap while maintaining "a sound that's current yet also classic". Carey further released multiple dances remixes of "You're Mine (Eternal)", including the Jump Smokers Radio Remix, Jump Smokers Extended Remix, and Jermaine Dupri X Kurd Maverick Germany To Southside Remix. Additional remixes by Fedde le Grand, Gregor Salto and Funkin ' Matt, and Chus and Ceballos were released on March 15.

스콘석(Stone of Scone) 또는 기적의 돌(Stone of Destiny)은 여러 세기에 걸쳐 스코틀랜드 군주의 대관식에 쓰이다가 나중에 영국, 그레이트브리튼 및 잉글랜드의 군주의 대관식에 쓰였던 직사각형 토막의 붉은 빛의 사암이다. 잉글랜드에서는 대관식 돌(Coronation Stone)로 부른다.

스콘석은 왕위 계승에 중요한 역할을 담당했던 스코틀랜드 사람들의 자부심을 대표하는 상징이다. 1296년에 이 돌은 잉글랜드에 빼앗겨 웨스트민스터 사원로 옮겨졌는데 이는 스코틀랜드 거주민들의 분노를 샀다. 1950년 성탄절에 네 명의 스코틀랜드 학생들이 이 돌을 훔쳐서 자기 동네로 옮겼으나 경찰에 붙잡히고 돌은 다시 원래 있던 지역으로 이송되었다. 1996년에 이 돌은 스코틀랜드에 있어야 한다는 영국 정부의 결정에 따라 다시 스코틀랜드에 안장되었다.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She simply packed her bags and left without a word to anyone in the office.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'simply' modifies the verb 'packed' and introduces no predicate nominal, so the hypothesis predicts silence while a minimiser reading predicts a firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The soup was just lukewarm and nobody at the table wanted to send it back.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'just' modifies a predicate adjective rather than reducing a subject to a bare nominal category, which the hypothesis's minimiser clause requires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He merely glanced at the report before tossing it into the recycling bin outside.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'merely' modifies the verb 'glanced' with no copula or predicate nominal, so the hypothesis predicts no peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They only arrived after midnight, long past the hour when the doors had been locked.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'only' restricts the verb 'arrived' instead of ascribing a category to the subject, which the hypothesis excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Shortly after midnight a sudden storm forced the entire crew to abandon the crossing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A determiner opens a subject noun phrase with no ascriptive frame around it, so the hypothesis predicts silence while a prenominal-slot reading predicts a firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The board rejected a proposal to relocate the factory closer to the coast last week.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An indefinite noun phrase sits in object position, which the hypothesis says is nearly silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The editor returned his manuscript with a long list of corrections scribbled in the margin.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A possessive determiner plus noun phrase in object position with no copula or as/like construal, so the hypothesis predicts no peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The train ran as far as the old mill before the engine finally gave out.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'as ... as' is a degree comparison rather than an as-construal characterising a subject, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I like the way she arranges the flowers on the table by the front window.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'like' is a verb of preference, not a simile or an as/like construal, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The new bridge is longer than the old one by almost forty metres.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'than' appears in a plain adjectival comparison and not in an ascriptive 'more than just a marker' frame, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: By spring some of the tiles on the roof had cracked during the winter frost.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'some' quantifies a subject partitive with no predication, so the hypothesis predicts silence while both a determiner reading and a minimiser reading predict a firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lights flickered twice, but the machine kept running until the morning shift arrived.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'but' coordinates two clauses and establishes no characterising frame, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The film was disappointing and far too long for the young audience it was made for.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A copula followed by predicate adjectives rather than a predicate nominal, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The mere mention of her name made the whole room go quiet for a moment.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'mere' modifies a subject noun phrase before the verb, so the retrospective ascriptive frame the hypothesis requires is absent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The only road out of the valley had been washed away by the flood waters.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'only' is a restrictive adjective inside the subject with no predicate nominal to its right, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The court accepted his testimony even though the timeline he gave was impossible.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An evidence-family noun in object position with no ascriptive frame, so the hypothesis predicts silence even though a lookahead reading predicts a peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lawyers questioned the evidence for hours before the judge finally sent the jury home.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The evidence-family noun is a bare object of a verb with no copula or construal, so the hypothesis predicts no peak while a lookahead reading predicts one.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Outside, as the temperature dropped, the pipes began to creak and groan.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'as' is a temporal conjunction of simultaneity, not a construal of the subject as a category, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: There is a small bakery on the corner next to the old pharmacy and the post office.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Existential 'is' introduces a new entity instead of characterising a subject, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: By the time the crew reached the summit the weather had turned. They had left the base camp two days earlier with enough food for a week, and the chief guide had checked every rope and lamp himself. Nobody had expected the wind to pick up so quickly, and nobody had packed a spare tent cover. They simply waited in the lee of a boulder, sharing what little water remained, while the guide counted the hours and watched the clouds. When the wind finally eased they packed up and started down, more tired than frightened, and they reached the hut before dark. The hut keeper gave them hot tea and a dry corner to sleep in.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long narrative whose only minimiser modifies a verb and whose only comparatives modify adjectives, with no predicate nominal anywhere, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The recent study offers an explanation for the anomaly that few economists had considered.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A copula-like verb of the kind the hypothesis names ('offers an analysis') followed by an indefinite predicate nominal with a non-evidence noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her refusal to sign struck the committee as a deliberate insult to its chairman.

readings.explanation: Fires where a sentence stops merely mentioning something and starts characterising it: the slot just before a predicate nominal after a copula or copula-like verb ('the film was a disaster', 'the memo was a clear example', 'This paper offers an analysis', 'counted as a clear sign'), after an as/like construal ('widely seen as a turning point', 'read him like an open scroll', 'more than just a marker'), or after a minimiser that reduces a subject to a bare category ('merely', 'just', 'only', 'simply', 'nothing but', 'no more than'). It does not care which noun fills the slot (swapping 'example' for 'photo', 'table', 'disaster' or 'evidence' leaves the peak unchanged) and the same noun phrase in subject or object position is nearly silent, so the mechanism is retrospective: it reads the ascriptive frame already built by the preceding words, while its Jacobian lens and ablation read out the abstract characterisation nouns that typically fill such a slot (evidence, example, indication, acknowledgment, manifestation, testimony) rather than one specific upcoming token.

A broad prenominal-slot neuron: the real trigger is the function word that opens a noun phrase anywhere in the clause (a, an, some, their, his, mere, usual, vivid), and the ascriptive examples only dominate the scan because expository text has many predicate nominals - it predicts the same firing when that noun phrase is a subject or an object.

A minimiser/exclusive detector: the pole tracks the lexical class {mere, merely, just, only, simply, but, some, no more than} rather than any predication, so it should fire just as hard when such a word modifies a verb or an adjective ('he merely glanced', 'merely tired') and stay quiet on 'was a disaster' or 'seen as a turning point' where no minimiser occurs.

A lookahead neuron preparing the evidence/testimony noun family, since the Jacobian lens and the pole's ablation both push exactly those nouns and the peak sits one or two tokens before the noun would land - it predicts that swapping the head noun after the slot changes the activation, which is the discriminator this hypothesis denies.
